title: GDScript: Rework ownership of external parsers
body:
## What problem(s) does this PR solve? - Works towards fixing the root cause and outdated errors from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/122821 (not a full fix) - Should help address race conditions when LSP and the editor are competing for the same AST (see https://github.com/godotengine/godot-vscode-plugin/issues/1007 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/94843 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/118621 https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/118612) I have not been able to reproduce those myself yet, so might need confirmation from someone who has but a theoretical breakdown is in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118615 - Works towards reducing complexity around the compilation toolchain. - Supersedes and closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/118615 ## Additional information > [!NOTE] > For everything I say here: TIWAGOS, this stuff is complex if not convoluted. The PR is risky AF, there is no way to get this stuff solved without taking those risks though. I'm confident that what I came up with here is able to solve all edge cases, even if this PR misses to address any particular one. Currently parser ownership is solved through two ways: - The main parser is on the stack. - External parsers are managed using ref counting (`GDScriptParserRef`), the refs are owned by other parsers which depended on the parser (`GDScriptParser::depended_parsers`). (The keen eyed one might spot the potential for cyclic refs which keeps parsers alive for longer than intended, that's were the outdated parsers from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/122821 originate) - In addition a non-owning reference to external parsers is registered with `GDScriptCache` for lookup. Since `GDScriptCache` is a singleton this makes the analyzer not thread safe. This PR moves away from refcounting, cyclic deps between scripts are supported so a proper ref counting scheme that ensures intended lifetimes is non trivial. Instead the external parsers are owned by the stack which also owns the main parser. I called the container for that `GDScriptCompilationUnit` in lack of better terms, open for suggestions :shrug: - Tested against the MRP from https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/94871 - Aiming for early inclusion in 4.9 ### Helpful for understanding - I started putting new compilation related code into a `toolchain` subfolder. I personally prefer small files and structured folders and the main folder of the GDScript module has IMHO grown too big. If I'm going against some project philosophy with this feel free to let me know and I'll begrudgingly flatten that out. - This PR removes a lot of code without replacement which might give the impression that parsers should have a long lifetime. This is not the case in my reading. Since d36d7e2a1c83141a3051d2c24b01c9a9e6104f89 the only references are hold in the other `GDScriptParsers` and would get freed when the main parser is freed through the stack. This just breaks down with cyclic refs and all the other code seems to be ducktape to patch that up. - The main parser is not part of the compilation unit (for now, I had a more elaborate version of these changes in the works but it grew too big), so cyclic deps can still result in multiple parsers for the same source code being part of the compilation. - The previous role of `ensure_cached_external_parser_for_class` was to lookup the parser for a class, while bypassing the lookup mechanism in `GDScriptCache` (which probably caused issues with outdated parsers in the past already). To do that it would look through all `depended_parsers` starting from the main parser on the stack. The method also had some caching for that sprinkled in. This is now trivialized since the entire transitive hull is indexed in `GDScriptCompilationUnit` - Feel free to ask if I missed explaining some stuff! ## The bigger picture This PR has some rough edges, I tried marking those with `HACK` comments. As mentioned above I had a bigger version in the works, but it's gotten too big and I don't think all oddities can be ironed out in one step. Amongst others it included more stringent path normalization, rework of canonical content, removal of the shallow script concept and more responsibilities moved into `GDScriptCompilationUnit`. I'll put a highlevel architecture diagram of what I'm going for here as reference in case it makes something more clear.
